sources.title: Human Security of Border Communities in Covalima, Bobonaro and RAEOA, Timor-Leste: Mapping and Assessment Report
sources.organization: Institute for Peace, Conflict and Social Studies, Universidade Nacional Timor Lorosa’e; commissioned by UNICEF and IOM
sources.temporal_coverage: Participatory assessment fieldwork in 2023; includes historical examples, including a 2021 displacement event.
sources.methodology: Qualitative mapping through 2023 focus groups, interviews and workshops in 23 border villages.
sources.limitations: Sampled participant accounts, not prevalence or climate-attribution analysis.

sources.title: Climate Rationale for Water, Sanitation and Hygiene Services in Timor-Leste
sources.organization: IVL Swedish Environmental Research Institute and UNICEF Timor-Leste
sources.temporal_coverage: Climate and WASH policy/risk review published August 2025; projections vary by stated scenario and horizon.
sources.methodology: Climate and WASH policy/literature review with expert task-force validation and a June 2025 workshop.
sources.limitations: Mixed data vintages; the cited water-dispute evidence is from 2017, not a current conflict assessment.

sources.title: UNICEF Timor-Leste Annual Report 2024: Action and Impact for Every Child
sources.methodology: UNICEF annual programme reporting of activities and outputs.
sources.limitations: Implementer-reported outputs; expected water benefits are not measured impacts.

sources.title: Mercy Corps, EU, and KOICA hand over Early Warning System devices to DNMG
sources.temporal_coverage: Early-warning handover and project descriptions reported in March 2024.
sources.methodology: Local news report on project handover and statements by implementing partners.
sources.limitations: Descriptive reporting; the article gives inconsistent counts for supported PREPARADU sucos.

sources.title: European Union and Mercy Corps celebrate successful conclusion of Maloa Urban Resilience Initiative Program
sources.temporal_coverage: Implementer-reported programme outputs at June 2024 close-out.
sources.methodology: EU and Mercy Corps close-out account of programme outputs.
sources.limitations: Implementer-reported capacity and works; no independent impact evaluation.

claims.locator: Printed p. 35, ‘Climate and food security’; community account from Gildapil, Bobonaro.
claims.paraphrase: Participants reported rainy-season landslides and floods destroying farms in Saburai, Tapo-Memo, Gildapil and Lebos (Bobonaro); Gildapil participants described hunger after maize loss.
institutions: Institute for Peace, Conflict and Social Studies, UNTL
claims.limitations: Qualitative participant accounts; no event attribution or prevalence estimate.

claims.locator: Printed p. 22, ‘Environmental security’, RAEOA community findings.
claims.paraphrase: In RAEOA, wet-season landslides in Bene-Ufe damaged roads, settlements and farms; flooding and landslides displaced 280 families around Nibin, Usitaqueno, in 2021.
institutions: Institute for Peace, Conflict and Social Studies, UNTL
claims.limitations: Retrospective, qualitative assessment; not a municipality-wide estimate.

claims.locator: Printed pp. 18–19, ‘Community security’, Tapo-Memo and cross-community resource disputes.
claims.paraphrase: The report describes disputes over water, land and livestock; at Tapo-Memo, unequal irrigation access to the shared Malibaka River raised concern about possible future water conflict.
claims.limitations: The assessment does not attribute these disputes to climate change.
claims.source_stated_fcv_link: The report identifies unequal river access as a possible water-conflict pathway, without attributing it to climate change.
claims.source_stated_fcv_locator: Printed pp. 18–19, ‘Community security’, paragraph on water, land and livestock disputes and Tapo-Memo’s Malibaka River access.

claims.locator: Printed pp. 37–38, ‘Pathways to resilience’, environmental security examples.
claims.paraphrase: Communities reportedly protected 80 water resources in RAEOA; Usi Taqueno residents fenced and cleaned springs, while Saburai protected water distribution through tara bandu.
claims.limitations: Community practices are reported, not independently evaluated for sustained impact.

claims.locator: Printed p. 25, flood exposure discussion under ‘Impacts on communities’.
claims.paraphrase: The WASH climate assessment says all municipalities face flood exposure; the largest numbers exposed to extreme floods are in Bobonaro and Dili, followed by Ainaro and Baucau.
claims.limitations: Underlying exposure-data vintage and municipal denominators are not restated in this passage.

claims.locator: Printed pp. 4 and 26, summary and ‘Impacts on communities’ sections.
claims.paraphrase: The assessment expects drought and extreme rainfall to worsen water insecurity, heighten competition and lengthen women’s trips to collect water, with unsafe sources increasing disease risk.
claims.limitations: Risk narrative, not measured future outcomes; no named municipality is given for this pathway.

claims.locator: Printed p. 26, water-competition discussion and citation to ACAPS (2017).
claims.paraphrase: Within its climate-risk discussion, the report cites a 2017 ACAPS finding that increased competition for limited water resulted in disputes within communities.
claims.limitations: The cited observation is from 2017; no current named conflict or violence prevalence is established.
claims.source_stated_fcv_link: The assessment places reported community disputes after increased competition for limited water in its climate-risk narrative, while citing older ACAPS evidence.
claims.source_stated_fcv_locator: Printed p. 26, ‘Impacts on communities’, paragraph on competition for limited water and disputes; footnote 38 cites ACAPS (2017).

claims.paraphrase: UNICEF reports community catchment-management expansion to 35 additional sub-villages in Ainaro and Viqueque, implemented by 70 trained residents and nearly 350 other community members, including women and youth.
claims.limitations: Annual programme reporting; activities are not an independent resilience evaluation.

claims.locator: Printed p. 39, infrastructure outputs and expected dry-season water pathway.
claims.paraphrase: The 532 built nature-based structures (45 ponds, 313 terraces and 174 check dams) were reported to retain at least 12,567 m³ in one rainfall event; dry-season replenishment is expected, not measured.
claims.limitations: Retention capacity and expected replenishment are UNICEF-reported; no monitored dry-season effect is supplied.

claims.locator: Article paragraphs on PREPARADU/Maloa project locations and the 16-station system handover.
claims.paraphrase: Sixteen early-warning devices were handed to DNMG; disaster committees were supported in Dili sucos. The article says 15 PREPARADU sucos but lists 16, including six Maloa sites: Villa Verde, Motael, Colmera, Campo Alor, Bairo Pite and Dare.
claims.limitations: Descriptive reporting; the listed PREPARADU suco count is internally inconsistent.

claims.locator: Close-out account paragraphs describing household, business and infrastructure results in the Maloa watershed.
claims.paraphrase: EU/Mercy Corps report 537 households with improved shock-preparation capacities, 1,284 people with climate-resilience knowledge, and 68 flood/landslide mitigation or adaptation works in the Maloa watershed.
claims.limitations: Implementer-reported outputs and capacity, not independently evaluated loss reduction or peace outcomes.

access_audit.locator: Complete 72-page report; village methods, climate/food/environmental security findings, community-security findings and resilience pathways.
access_audit.notes: The report describes 2023 participatory fieldwork and separately identifies several events as historical or participant-reported.
access_audit.reuse_terms: No separate open licence verified; concise attributed paraphrases only.

access_audit.locator: Complete 44-page climate rationale; municipality flood discussion and pp. 25–26 water/WASH impacts.
access_audit.notes: The report combines literature, policy review and stakeholder validation; water-dispute material is attributed to an earlier ACAPS source.
access_audit.reuse_terms: Copyright is stated; no separate open licence verified; concise attributed paraphrases only.

access_audit.locator: Complete 27-page annual report; printed pp. 38–39, ‘Climate change’.
access_audit.notes: Annual-report passages distinguish built infrastructure and storage capacity from expected dry-season water effects.
access_audit.reuse_terms: No separate open licence verified; concise attributed paraphrases only.

access_audit.locator: Full article, 27 March 2024; paragraphs describing project areas, committees and device handover.
access_audit.notes: The article lists 16 sucos after saying PREPARADU supported 15; the discrepancy is retained rather than reconciled.
access_audit.reuse_terms: No separate open licence verified; concise attributed paraphrases only.

access_audit.locator: Full EU close-out article, 13 June 2024; paragraphs reporting Maloa household, knowledge and works outputs.
access_audit.notes: Implementer/partner-reported programme completion data; no independent impact evaluation is presented.
access_audit.reuse_terms: No separate open licence verified; concise attributed paraphrases only.

access_audit.locator: Complete 88-page CCRI-DRM narrative and methodology; municipality-specific results are primarily presented through the companion platform.
access_audit.notes: The PDF was read but does not transcribe accessible named-municipality rankings in its narrative. The companion geospatial platform was inaccessible through the web reader and direct HTTPS request; no rankings from secondary summaries were used.
access_audit.reuse_terms: No separate open licence verified; no findings extracted beyond audit/search context.

access_audit.locator: 2025 UN Common Country Analysis PDF download.
access_audit.notes: The web reader rejected the approximately 28.6 MB document for exceeding its content-size limit; no findings from it were used.
access_audit.reuse_terms: Not assessed because the document could not be accessed.

search_audit.query: Timor-Leste 2024 2025 floods drought subnational municipalities official report UN OCHA FAO
search_audit.outcome: Found named village-level climate impacts in the 2024 UNICEF/IOM border-community assessment and municipality-level flood exposure in the 2025 WASH climate rationale. The 2026 CCRI-DRM narrative was read, but municipal scores were not available in its text and the companion platform could not be accessed.

search_audit.query: Timor-Leste climate conflict security community water disputes land-resource primary report
search_audit.outcome: Found source-stated water/land/livestock disputes and a possible shared-river water-conflict pathway at Tapo-Memo, plus a WASH climate-risk synthesis citing older community water disputes. Neither source attributes a broader armed conflict to climate change.

search_audit.query: Timor-Leste violence insecurity conflict blocking climate adaptation disaster response access project report
search_audit.outcome: No inspected source documented violence or insecurity directly blocking a named climate-adaptation operation. The border assessment reports climate/natural-disaster interruptions to market access and damaged roads affecting services; these are not treated as conflict blocking adaptation.

search_audit.query: Timor-Leste community climate adaptation resilience results Ainaro Viqueque Dili early warning 2024 report
search_audit.outcome: Found UNICEF-reported community catchment structures in Ainaro/Viqueque, Dili early-warning and disaster-committee support, and Maloa watershed resilience outputs. These are reported outputs rather than independently evaluated impacts.

gaps: The 2026 UNICEF CCRI-DRM narrative does not expose named-municipality scores in accessible text, and its companion geospatial platform could not be accessed; no rankings from secondary summaries were used.
The border-community study is qualitative and based on selected villages; its reported resource disputes are not attributed to climate change.
The climate/WASH assessment combines varying data vintages and cites 2017 ACAPS material for water disputes; it is not a current conflict or violence assessment.
No inspected source shows insecurity or violence directly blocking a named climate-adaptation project; disaster-related access interruption is documented but is not a reverse FCV-to-climate finding.
UNICEF and project close-out results are implementer-reported; expected water replenishment and broader resilience or peace effects were not independently evaluated.
TATOLI says 15 PREPARADU sucos were supported but enumerates 16; the count was not reconciled.
